props.command: Four athletes get called 'the greatest' in four different sports, but I don't think 'greatness' means the same thing for each of them. Can you (1) break down the actual shape of each one's dominance — a streak, a career total, a multi-format run, a fixed peak — and (2) tell me which of those four mechanisms is hardest to sustain, with the real numbers to back it up?
output: a streak that broke, then rebuilt itself
a goal total still climbing toward 1,000
a career split across closed and open formats
a peak that's frozen in history

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Jash Shah, and this video is based on four legendary sports careers — Tony Ferguson, Cristiano Ronaldo, Rohit Sharma, and Roger Federer. Four athletes, four sports, all called the greatest ever. But greatness doesn't mean the same thing four times. Today we grade the actual shape of dominance.

beats.narration: A UFC streak. A five-club goal chase. A four-format career. A closed Grand Slam count. Same word — greatness — four completely different mechanics.

props.title: Tony Ferguson — 12 straight, then a second title

data.current: Reigning Misfits Boxing Middleweight Champion (won Dec 20, 2025)

beats.narration: Twelve straight UFC wins, 2013 to 2019 — Rio, Kikuno, Castillo, Tibau, Thomson, Barboza, Vannata, dos Anjos, Kevin Lee for an interim title, Pettis, Cerrone. Then a hard stretch. Today? Misfits Boxing's middleweight champion. The comeback is the streak's second act.

beats.narration: Four formats, one career. Eleven thousand five hundred ODI runs, including the only three double-centuries ever and the world record, two sixty-four. Four thousand two thirty-one T20I runs — the most ever, closed in twenty twenty-four. Seventy-three hundred IPL runs, five titles as Mumbai's captain. Two formats retired. Two still running.

beats.narration: Twenty Grand Slam singles titles. It was the record when he set it. Djokovic has since reached twenty-four. Federer's number is frozen — the peak closed the day he retired.

artifactLines: Ferguson: a 12-fight streak, a hard stretch, a second title in boxing.
Ronaldo: 976 goals across five clubs and Portugal — 450 at Real Madrid, 145 at Man Utd — still climbing toward 1,000.
Rohit Sharma: one career, four formats — Test and T20I closed, ODI and IPL still open.
Federer: 20 Grand Slams, a peak frozen since 2022 — since passed by Djokovic's 24.

beats.narration: Four shapes of dominance: a streak that broke and rebuilt itself, a goal chase still climbing, a career split across closing and open formats, and a peak frozen in history. Greatness isn't one shape. It's whichever one you're grading.
